0.value:
The gather_sentence node collects fragments of text until a sentence ends, then sends the whole sentence.

Speech recognition and language models emit text a fragment at a time. None of it is a sentence, and most of what you want to do needs one.

WHERE A SENTENCE ENDS:
With 'auto sentence end' on (the default), a fragment that ENDS in . ? ! ; or :
completes the sentence and it is sent, that fragment included. So does a fragment ending in two dashes, or in two line breaks, and one ending in a closing bracket when the sentence began with an opening one. An ellipsis (...) does not end a sentence. The punctuation has to be the fragment's last character - 'changing. ' with a space after does not count.

'force string end' sends whatever has been collected, whenever the patch decides - an empty string if nothing has been. A fragment that is exactly
'<backspace>' removes the last fragment collected (or does nothing when nothing
has been).

SPACES:
Fragments are joined exactly as they arrive - no space is added between them. Recognition output usually carries its own spaces; if yours does not, tick 'enforce spaces', which puts a space between fragments that meet without one - but not before a full stop, comma or other closing punctuation, nor after an
opening bracket. A '<backspace>' removes the fragment together with the space
added in front of it.

LINE BREAKS:
'end on return' ends the sentence at a line break: what came before it is sent, and what follows starts the next sentence. Line breaks never appear in what is sent.

LEAVING THINGS OUT:
'skip framed by' takes a single character and removes everything between a
pair of it - so with '*', 'it is *laughs* cold.' is sent as 'it is  cold.'.
Stage directions or annotations in the stream do not end up in the sentence.

SYNTAX:
gather_sentence

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

string in:
The fragments.

force string end:
Send what has been collected now.

enforce spaces / auto sentence end / end on return / skip framed by:
As above.

OUTPUTS:

sentences out:
The assembled sentence.

RELATED:
string_builder collects until it is asked, rather than until a sentence ends. fifo_string keeps a rolling window of recent sentences. text_change reports only the words in a stream that are new.
